newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF says Thai measures on baht 'appropriate'.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF says Thai measures on baht 'appropriate'.

text.p: Measures taken by Thai authorities on the baht were appropriate, Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Wednesday.
He also said Japan would keep in close contact with Thai authorities on currencies, as it had been doing in the past.
Mitsuzuka said he had heard that the Bank of Thailand (BOT) had announced on Wednesday that the country had switched to a "managed float" policy on the baht.
He also acknowledged a Thai statement that said the measure would help overall economic development in Thailand by giving its economy more flexibility.
"We accept the statement as it is. We think Thai authorities have taken appropriate measures," Mitsuzuka said.
"We think it is important to keep close contact (with Thai authorities) as in the past," he added.
Asked whether the Japanese government would give financial support to help the Thai baht, Mitsuzuka said he would not answer such questions.
On other issues, he said MOF will come up with basic guidelines on 1998/99 budget requests to be made by other ministries in time for cabinet ministers to approve the guidelines on July 8.
Japanese ministries usually submit budget requests for the next fiscal year to MOF by the end of August.
